checkpoints.title: IP Is the Destination; the Port Is the Service Entrance
checkpoints.prompt: On the same EC2 instance, SSH succeeds but only HTTPS using port 443 fails. Select one item to check separately first.

choices.text: HTTPS port permission and service listening
choices.explanation: Correct. Even with the same IP, the service entrance is different.

choices.text: Conclude that HTTPS is also working normally based only on the successful SSH connection.
choices.explanation: The port and the higher-level stage are different.

choices.text: Treat the IP address as the port number.
choices.explanation: The IP is the destination; the port is the service entrance.

checkpoints.title: Choose TCP or UDP Based on Where Delivery Responsibility Lies
checkpoints.prompt: The value of old audio that arrives late is low, and the application can be designed to handle loss. Select one correct comparison.

choices.text: Consider UDP and decide at the application layer how to handle any necessary loss and ordering measures.
choices.explanation: Correct. UDP does not guarantee these properties.

choices.text: UDP always guarantees retransmission and ordering.
choices.explanation: These are not standard UDP guarantees.

choices.text: Obtain retransmission guarantees using only the port number.
choices.explanation: The port does not change delivery characteristics.

checkpoints.title: TLS Handles the Communication Channel, While HTTP Handles Application Semantics
checkpoints.prompt: When a user opens a product page in a browser, the TLS handshake succeeds, but HTTP 404 is returned. Choose one place the operations team should investigate first.

choices.text: Routing corresponding to the HTTP URL path or the target product page
choices.explanation: Correct. 404 is an HTTP-stage response.

choices.text: Verification of the TLS certificate name
choices.explanation: TLS has already succeeded.

choices.text: DNS name resolution
choices.explanation: Because the request reached HTTP, DNS did not fail in this observation.

checkpoints.title: Choose the next stage based on evidence, not changes
checkpoints.prompt: DNS and TCP succeeded, but the connection stopped because the TLS certificate hostname did not match. Select one item to check next.

choices.text: The certificate’s SAN (Subject Alternative Name), expiration, and trust chain
choices.explanation: Correct. Check the TLS verification conditions.

choices.text: Only the body of HTTP 404
choices.explanation: The HTTP body has not been retrieved because TLS is not complete.

choices.text: Open all ports
choices.explanation: This does not fix the certificate name mismatch.

choices.text: Which service on that IP address to deliver traffic to
choices.explanation: Correct. The port and protocol distinguish the service entry point.

choices.text: The packet’s destination on the network
choices.explanation: An IP address is used to identify the destination.

choices.text: The expiration date of the TLS certificate
choices.explanation: The certificate expiration date is part of TLS validation.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations administrator is reviewing a configuration in which SSH and HTTPS listen on the same IP address of a single EC2 instance. Choose one thing that cannot be distinguished by the destination IP address alone but can be distinguished by the port number.
finalQuestions.title: IP addresses and ports

choices.text: Permission for port 443 and service listening on that port
choices.explanation: Correct. IP reachability and permission and listening on a specific port must be checked separately.

choices.text: Only the S3 bucket name
choices.explanation: The bucket name does not indicate that the target service is listening on a port.

choices.text: Only KMS key rotation
choices.explanation: KMS key management is not a check of this TCP service entry point.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations administrator is investigating why SSH provided by the same EC2 instance is reachable, but HTTPS on port 443 is not. After confirming that the address is reachable, choose one thing to investigate next.
finalQuestions.title: Checking the service entry point

choices.text: TCP exchanges byte streams after establishing a connection with the peer.
choices.explanation: It transfers byte streams between the two connected endpoints.

choices.text: If TCP transmission is acknowledged, you can conclude that the order has been successfully registered.
choices.explanation: Acknowledgment of the transfer does not guarantee that the application successfully registered the order.

choices.text: TCP manages ordering and retransmits lost data.
choices.explanation: It delivers an ordered byte stream to the receiving application.

finalQuestions.prompt: A developer of an order service uses TCP so that the server receives the byte stream sent by the client in order. Select one incorrect statement about TCP connections.
finalQuestions.title: TCP Properties

choices.text: When using UDP, decide where handling of ordering, retransmission, and loss will be performed.
choices.explanation: The application determines the required ordering and behavior when data is missing.

choices.text: UDP always guarantees ordering and retransmission, so no additional design is necessary.
choices.explanation: UDP does not provide those guarantees.

choices.text: Changing the port number provides delivery guarantees.
choices.explanation: A port identifies a service; it does not change delivery guarantees.

choices.text: Because continuing to wait for audio after its playback deadline increases latency, consider a design that allows missing audio.
choices.explanation: For live audio, consider both waiting for expired audio and the impact of missing audio.

finalQuestions.prompt: A delivery operator is considering a configuration that uses UDP for live audio. Delayed, old audio has little value, and the behavior when data is missing is determined by the application. Select two incorrect statements about decisions when using UDP.
finalQuestions.title: UDP Responsibilities

choices.text: For live display and file distribution, decide separately how much loss and retransmission delay can be tolerated.
choices.explanation: The priorities for latency and data integrity differ by use case.

choices.text: Applying TLS automatically resolves loss and ordering, so there is no need to consider the communication method separately.
choices.explanation: Encryption and delivery characteristics are separate. The presence or absence of TLS alone cannot determine whether delivery is suitable for the use case.

choices.text: For file distribution, choose a method that can verify that the received content matches the original data.
choices.explanation: When loss is unacceptable, verify the integrity of the received result.

finalQuestions.prompt: A developer is investigating whether a common communication method can be adopted for live display and file distribution. The impact of missing data and the time available to wait for retransmission differ by use case. Select one incorrect statement about choosing a communication method.
finalQuestions.title: Choosing a Communication Method

choices.text: The TLS connection was established, and the party that returned the HTTP response indicated that the requested resource could not be found.
choices.explanation: Correct. A 404 is an HTTP response, not a TLS failure.

choices.text: The TLS certificate validation failed because there was a 404
choices.explanation: Receiving an HTTP 404 normally means that the TLS stage was completed.

choices.text: Changing only DNS will always resolve the 404
choices.explanation: The cause could be HTTP routing or application resources after DNS succeeds.

finalQuestions.prompt: A developer checking a connection in a browser receives an HTTP 404 after the TLS handshake completes. Select one conclusion that can be drawn from this result.
finalQuestions.title: TLS and HTTP

choices.text: Whether orders.example is included in the certificate’s SAN (Subject Alternative Name).
choices.explanation: Correct. Verify that the connection name matches the certificate name.

choices.text: The certificate’s validity period and trust chain
choices.explanation: Correct. These are conditions for TLS validation.

choices.text: Only the body of the HTTP 404
choices.explanation: Because TLS has not completed, the HTTP body is not useful for diagnosis.

choices.text: Only the application’s JSON response format
choices.explanation: This is not part of the preliminary TLS certificate validation.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations staff member reports that when connecting to orders.example on the order page, the browser displays an error saying that the certificate name does not match. No HTTP response has been received. Select two items to check when validating the TLS certificate.
finalQuestions.title: Certificate Validation

choices.text: Check the HTTP routing of the application or reverse proxy
choices.explanation: 404 is an item to investigate when locating resources at the HTTP layer.

choices.text: Conclude that disabling TLS will guarantee that the HTTP resource is found
choices.explanation: Correct. Disabling TLS will not fix the HTTP path or routing.

choices.text: Record the requested path and HTTP method
choices.explanation: This fixes the reproduction conditions on the HTTP side.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations staff member is investigating an order API. The TLS handshake completed successfully, and GET /orders returns HTTP 404. Select one judgment that is incorrect when investigating the cause.
finalQuestions.title: HTTP Responsibility

choices.text: The queried name and the IP returned by DNS
choices.explanation: Correct. This fixes the destination for subsequent communication.

choices.text: How far the connection reached among the TCP connection, TLS verification, and HTTP response
choices.explanation: Correct. This narrows down the first stage at which the failure occurred.

choices.text: The result of opening all ports because the cause was unknown
choices.explanation: Opening all ports reduces security and makes the diagnostic evidence ambiguous.

choices.text: Record only whether it succeeded, without recording the name or port
choices.explanation: Without reproduction conditions, you cannot compare the results after a change.

finalQuestions.prompt: A user cannot open the order site orders.example. The operations engineer does not yet know at which stage of communication the problem occurred. Select two pieces of information to use for the initial isolation.
finalQuestions.title: Step-by-Step Diagnosis

choices.text: Check whether the destination port is listening and whether the port is allowed
choices.explanation: A refusal is a clue to check service listening status or reachability conditions.

choices.text: Decide that redeploying the HTTP application will definitely solve the problem
choices.explanation: Correct. Evidence from the TCP stage alone does not establish that the HTTP application is the cause.

choices.text: Record the connected IP, port, and source
choices.explanation: This is necessary to observe the same conditions again.

choices.text: Expose all ports to all sources without checking the required scope
choices.explanation: Correct. Abandoning least privilege does not identify the cause.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations engineer confirmed that the order API name resolves to the expected IP, but the TCP connection to port 443 is refused. There is no HTTP response. Select two incorrect next investigation approaches.
finalQuestions.title: Investigating a TCP Rejection

choices.text: Retest using the same source, name, port, and request as before the change
choices.explanation: Correct. This keeps the comparison conditions consistent and validates the hypothesis.

choices.text: End the observation without recording anything because it succeeded once
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish an accidental success from a permanent fix.

choices.text: Verify that access is limited to the required sources and ports
choices.explanation: Correct. This confirms that the fix did not create new excessive exposure.

choices.text: Permanently allow all ports because failure is concerning
choices.explanation: This loses least privilege and makes the cause of the incident unclear.

finalQuestions.prompt: The operations engineer changed the security group so that the order site’s EC2 instance can be reached on port 443 from the internal monitoring source. Select two ways to verify the effect of the change and the permitted scope.
finalQuestions.title: Validating the Fix

choices.text: Record the queried name, the resolver in use, and the error returned.
choices.explanation: This helps clarify the failure at the DNS stage.

choices.text: Conclude that reissuing the TLS certificate will definitely fix the DNS failure.
choices.explanation: Correct. A TLS certificate does not directly fix the cause of DNS resolution.

choices.text: After fixing the DNS configuration, verify the same name resolution again.
choices.explanation: This verifies the result of the fix at the same stage.

choices.text: Conclude that fixing HTTP 404 first will also make name resolution succeed.
choices.explanation: Correct. The process stops at DNS before reaching HTTP.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations engineer confirmed that the name of the ordering site could not be resolved by DNS and that the browser had not obtained the destination IP address. Select the two actions that are incorrect at this point.
finalQuestions.title: Do Not Confuse the Layers

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.text: Treat names, IPs, ports, TLS, and HTTP as separate points of verification, and narrow down the incident using the necessary evidence.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Without confusing the destination, service entry point, encryption, and HTTP processing, select the next check based on the observed results.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Distinguish what IP addresses and ports refer to.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Compare TCP and UDP based on the required delivery properties.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Treat TLS verification and HTTP responses as separate stages.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Choose the next diagnostic step based on the stage already observed.

blocks.label: IP is the destination; the port is the service entry point
blocks.text: An IP address represents the destination on the network to which packets are delivered. Even when multiple services exist on the same host or network interface, the IP address alone does not determine which service receives the packet.

blocks.label: IP is the destination; the port is the service entry point
blocks.text: For TCP and UDP, port numbers distinguish service entry points. Security group rules also allow traffic by combining the protocol, port range, and source or destination. Port 443 is commonly used for HTTPS, but HTTPS is not necessarily on port 443.

blocks.label: IP is the destination; the port is the service entry point
blocks.text: Being able to SSH to an IP does not necessarily mean that you can connect to the web service at the same IP. For each service, check the port it uses, the settings along the path that allow that port, and whether the process is listening.

steps.label: IP is the destination; the port is the service entry point

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: SSH to the same EC2 instance succeeds from the administration terminal, but only the application’s HTTPS connection fails.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Confirm that the IP returned by DNS is the expected EC2 instance.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: If the design uses TCP 443, confirm permission from the source to port 443 and confirm reachability.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Confirm that the process on EC2 is listening on that port and can present a certificate.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Do not judge the entire HTTPS path to be healthy based on successful SSH; investigate the service entry point and higher-level stages separately.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If you know the IP address, you can connect to any application on that host.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: An IP address only identifies the destination. You can connect to the target service only when the protocol, port, permissions, and service listener are all in place.

steps.label: This is incorrect and here is the correction

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: IP addresses and ports are separate factors to consider.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: The HTTPS port is determined by the configuration; do not assume only the default value.

blocks.label: Choose TCP or UDP based on where delivery responsibility lies
blocks.text: TCP establishes a connection and provides a reliable byte stream using sequencing and retransmission. It is used for applications such as web applications, where missing requests or reordered data should not be handled as-is.

blocks.label: Choose TCP or UDP based on where delivery responsibility lies
blocks.text: UDP sends datagrams without establishing a connection. UDP itself does not guarantee delivery, ordering, or duplicate elimination, so when necessary, the application must design how to handle loss, ordering, and retransmission.

blocks.label: Choose TCP or UDP based on where delivery responsibility lies
blocks.text: Do not choose between protocols based only on “UDP is fast” or “TCP is safe.” First determine whether old data has value, whether loss is acceptable, and how waiting for retransmission affects the user experience.

steps.label: Choose TCP or UDP based on where delivery responsibility lies

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Some packets from a live audio stream arrive late.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Decide whether playing late-arriving audio is valuable and whether missing data needs to be recovered.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Choose whether to leave ordering and retransmission to the communication method or handle them in the application.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Evaluate the approach based on measured latency, loss, and impact on users.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can compare delivery guarantees and latency tolerance without choosing TCP/UDP by name.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Choosing UDP always results in low latency, so you do not need to consider ordering or loss.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: As a protocol, UDP does not guarantee ordering or retransmission. Even in a design that prioritizes low latency, you must decide where to compensate for loss.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: First, write down the required delivery, ordering, and retransmission properties.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: The application design is responsible for making up for what UDP lacks.

blocks.label: TLS handles the communication channel, while HTTP handles application meaning
blocks.text: TLS protects the communication channel between the client and server and verifies items such as the certificate name, validity period, and trust chain. If TLS verification fails, the connection usually stops before an HTTP request is sent.

blocks.label: TLS handles the communication channel, while HTTP handles application meaning
blocks.text: HTTP defines the meaning of request methods, the URI, status codes, and the body. A 404 response indicates that the target resource was not found as a result of processing an HTTP request. It is not at the same layer as a TLS failure or a DNS failure.

blocks.label: TLS handles the communication channel, while HTTP handles application meaning
blocks.text: When troubleshooting an HTTPS failure, start with the observations you obtained. For a certificate name mismatch, investigate TLS; for a 404, investigate HTTP routing or the application's resources. Do not repeatedly change a stage that has already succeeded.

steps.label: TLS handles the communication channel, while HTTP handles application meaning

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The browser displays a certificate name mismatch for orders.example and does not display an HTTP status code.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Confirm that the name resolution result and destination are as expected.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Check the certificate's SAN/CN, validity period, and trust chain.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Only after TLS validation succeeds, investigate the HTTP path and status code.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Do not treat the certificate problem as HTTP 404; it can be fixed at the TLS stage.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If HTTPS returns 404, the TLS certificate is also broken.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: 404 is an HTTP response after TLS succeeds. Certificate validation and HTTP resource discovery are separate failure stages.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: TLS success does not mean HTTP success.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Investigate what comes after the last successfully observed stage.

blocks.label: Choose the Next Step Based on Evidence, Not Changes
blocks.text: In network diagnostics, record the name entered by the user, the DNS response, the destination IP, the TCP connection to the port, TLS verification, and the HTTP response. While an earlier stage is failing, you cannot determine that a later stage is the cause.

blocks.label: Choose the Next Step Based on Evidence, Not Changes
blocks.text: Before broadening permissions or redeploying, choose an observation that can narrow the hypothesis to one possibility. For example, if the TCP connection is refused, check the destination IP, port, security group, and listener, and postpone changes to the HTTP application.

blocks.label: Choose the Next Step Based on Evidence, Not Changes
blocks.text: After making a correction, observe again using the same name, source, port, and request. Do not stop after a single coincidental success; keep a record that disproves or supports the hypothesis held before the change.

steps.label: Choose the Next Step Based on Evidence, Not Changes

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Only some users cannot connect to orders.example.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Compare the DNS responses and destination IPs for each user.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Record TCP, TLS, and HTTP in sequence under the same source conditions.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: After the minimum necessary change, test again under the same conditions to determine the scope of the impact.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can avoid risky trials such as opening all ports and limit the change to the first stage that failed.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If the cause is unknown, opening the security group completely first will speed up isolation.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Opening it completely introduces new effects and makes the evidence ambiguous. Check the required source, protocol, and port in relation to the hypothesis.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Treat each stage from DNS through HTTP as a separate observation point.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: After making a fix, observe again under the same conditions.
